title: The document shell
intro_p: By default `render` emits a bare HTML fragment — ready to pipe into something bigger. Passing `--title`, `--css`, `--head` or `--lang` switches the output to a finished document: the same fragment wrapped in a minimal HTML shell. With no flags the fragment is byte-identical to what oliver rendered alone.
fragment_p: A bare fragment — no shell flags:
fragment_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
title_p: `--title` wraps the fragment in the shell and sets `<title>`. The text is HTML-escaped for `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` — the data is untrusted:
css_p: `--css` adds a stylesheet link to the shell. Repeatable — links keep flag order — and the href passes through verbatim: URL or relative path, unvalidated. The consumer owns it.
document_p: The whole deal — one command, one finished document:
document_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json --title 'Verdict — dogbed' --css style.css Verdict — dogbed

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
xhtml_p: `--profile xhtml` swaps the HTML5 shell for XHTML 1.0 Strict: strict doctype, an http-equiv meta instead of `<meta charset>` (which is invalid XHTML), self-closing `<link … />` tags, and `xmlns` on the root element.
xhtml_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json -p xhtml --title 'Verdict' --css style.css Verdict

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
lang_p: `--lang` sets the document language on the shell's root element — what screen readers pick pronunciation rules from (WCAG 3.1.1, Level A). HTML5 gets `lang`; XHTML also gets `xml:lang`. The tag passes through verbatim, so pick a valid BCP 47 tag: `en`, `pt-BR`.
lang_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json --lang en --title 'Verdict — dogbed' | head -3
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
cap_p: `--max-output` caps the final document — shell included. Every output stage is bounded by the same value, so a runaway template or an escaping-heavy body dies the moment a write would cross the cap: over-limit output is never materialized. An emitted-byte ceiling is not a memory or CPU sandbox — embedders still need timeouts, concurrency limits, and OS-level resource controls:
cap_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json --title T --css style.css --max-output 250
dogbed: output exceeds --max-output (250)
gotcha1_p: Dogfood finding: data strings are Markdown source — `*`, backticks and `[label](url)` in a value render live. Mostly that is what you want; occasionally it eats characters you meant literally:
gotcha1_tr:
$ echo '{"t":"a *em* and `code` and [x](http://e.com)"}' | dogbed render note.knap -d -

a em and code and x
gotcha2_p: Dogfood finding: block markers count too — a value that opens with `# ` renders as a heading, `> ` as a quote. Markdown owns the whole stream, top to bottom:
gotcha2_tr:
$ echo '{"t":"# looks like a heading"}' | dogbed render note.knap -d -

looks like a heading
fix_p: The fix: the `escape_md` filter walks a value back to plain text — inline specials get backslash-escaped before Markdown ever sees them:
fix_tr:
$ cat note.knap {{ t | escape_md }} $ echo '{"t":"a *em* and `code` and [x](http://e.com)"}' | dogbed render note.knap -d -

a *em* and `code` and [x](http://e.com)
